aria: Quick follow-up on safetensors handoff + eager warmup compatibility — ran a canary and hit OOMs when loader tried hotstart on mixed safetensors+gz shards. Short dump: loader assumes contiguous offsets; compressed shards change in-mem map -> eviction thrash.

josh: Can you paste the minimal log + steps to repro?

aria: Logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-18T15:02:31Z WARN warmup: hotstart failed: mmap read beyond shard bounds
stack: warmup.hotstart -> loader.map_shard -> mmap_fault
model: mosaic-1.0 sharded(32) mixed-format
```
Repro: curl the canary bundle + run `pytest tests/warmup/test_hotstart.py::test_mixed_shard_hotstart --eager-warmup`. Hangs then OOMs in CI.

kai: Sounds like the handoff contract between weights-sourcer and loader is missing layout metadata. Our current handoff tuple is basically {shard_id, size, url, checksum} — not enough for mmap/hotstart that needs chunk layout or on-disk offsets.

maria: We need backward compatibility. Proposal: extend manifest with an optional `hotstart_layout` per shard and bump manifest version. New loaders will read it; old ones ignore it. No immediate breakage.

josh: Alternative: runtime probe shim in loader that reads first N bytes of each shard to detect format (safetensors header vs gzip magic vs custom packed). Less invasive but adds per-shard probing cost.

aria: Benchmarks: probing ~0.15–0.3ms/shard for local disk, ~5–20ms/shard for remote (depends on S3 range latency). Warmup is latency sensitive — for short lived warmups probing costs add up. Also ranged reads can be unreliable behind some proxies/CDNs.

kai: Tradeoffs: manifest field = one-time metadata fetch at manifest read; shim = zero-manifest-change but runtime overhead and brittle on stores that don't support range. Suggest both: manifest-first, probe fallback.

maria: Rollout plan idea: 1) Add manifest `hotstart_layout` optional field (no default enforcement). 2) Implement loader to consume manifest if present. 3) Add probe shim behind feature flag `EAGER_HOTSTART_PROBE=true` for clusters that need it. 4) Gradual canary.

deploy-bot: Canary config created: eng-ml-canary -> 10% hosts for 1h, if OK -> 50% at 6h. Will annotate PR with canary tag.

ops-bot: Please add metrics: `warmup_failure_count`, `warmup_probe_latency_ms_p50_p95`, and `hotstart_success_rate`. Alert if `warmup_failure_count > 5` in 1h.

aria: Sketch of detection pseudo-code for the shim:
```
function detect_shard_format(url, shard_id, manifest=None):
  if manifest and manifest.hotstart_layout and shard_id in manifest.hotstart_layout:
    return manifest.hotstart_layout[shard_id]  # explicit layout wins
  head = http_range_get(url, bytes=0-128)  # small probe, may be cached
  if head.startswith(b"safetensors") or b"safetensors" in head:
    return 'safetensors'
  if head.startswith(b"\x1f\x8b"):
    return 'gzip'
  return 'unknown'
```
Notes: need presigned URL reuse for probes, and fallback path if range not supported.

josh: Edgecases to test: signed URL expiry mid-probe, range-not-supported (HTTP 200 full-body returns), presign reuse, and truncated head. Also add unit tests for partial reads and mock S3 failures.

maria: Action items: aria -> PR for manifest schema + example bundles; kai -> loader shim prototype and perf microbench; josh -> test harness + S3 sim benchmarks; ops -> add canary metrics & alert rules. Release note copy: "loader: supports optional `hotstart_layout` in model manifest for eager hotstart; loader will fallback to probe-based detection when enabled via feature flag."

aria: I'll open the PR today and tag @eng-ml for review. Will include a minimal compatibility test and canary rollout plan. :thumbsup:

maria: Sounds good — prefer manifest-first approach. Thanks all. :eyes:
